method: TDD: rewrote tests/dom-test.js first, ran it against a missing ui.py to observe failure, then implemented.
Fixture is generated by a temporary Python stub that imports ui with characters carrying only a 'char' key, into a temp dir; site/ is never written.
Mutation testing: deliberately broke four behaviours in ui.py and confirmed the DOM test fails for each.
Static structural parse of the generated page (tag balance, class counts, aria-label uniqueness).

verifications.check: 21 character cards in order 我有爸媽姐妹弟哥和祖父母老師消防員警察醫生
every card button data-video = videos/<char>.mp4 and download = <char>字彩色筆順動畫.mp4
original nine reachable from a top quick row (9 quick buttons, correct targets)
8 word cards; 17 constituent buttons incl. duplicates (爸爸, 媽媽), each bound to its own video
modal open sets char/word label, src, download href + filename
replay rewinds to 0 and replays the same src
close button and Escape (cancel -> close) both pause and rewind
switching character pauses and rewinds the previous clip before loading the new one
rejected play() promise produces no unhandled rejection (process.on('unhandledRejection') fails the run)
generated HTML tag-balanced; no duplicate aria-labels across quick row, cards and word buttons
page_html raises ValueError naming missing characters if a word's character is absent
page_html normalises unordered/duplicated input to the canonical teaching order
mutation: uncaught play() rejection, no stop on close, deduped word buttons, wrong download name -> all four caught

findings.issue: An empty #current-word span still consumed a 12px flex gap in the dialog header, leaving a visible hole when a character was opened from a card rather than a word.
The temporary fixture directory was only removed on the success path, so a failing assertion leaked a directory into /tmp.
Switching to another character while the dialog is open must not leave the previous clip running or resume it mid-way; open() now always pauses and rewinds before assigning the new src.
findings.fix: stop() at the top of open(); mutation test confirms the assertion fails without it

findings.issue: On a ~375px phone the two-column word grid cannot fit 消防員's three 56px buttons on one row, so they wrap 2+1.
findings.rationale: Wrapping is centred and touch targets stay >=56px; forcing one column would break the requested 3-desktop/2-phone rhythm.

findings.issue: Characters and words are interpolated into HTML without escaping.
findings.rationale: Input is a curated CJK set defined in build.py/ui.py; there is no user-supplied path into the page.

findings.issue: ORDINALS covers words up to four characters; a longer word would raise IndexError at build time.
findings.rationale: Longest word is 消防員 (3). Failure would be loud at build time, not a silently wrong label.

findings.issue: The original nine can be played from both the quick row and their cards.
findings.rationale: Deliberate: only the 21 cards use .character-card, and the quick row uses distinct labels (快速播放「X」字筆順) so screen-reader users never see two identically named buttons.

findings.issue: npm test's second half (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests) currently errors because no interpreter on this machine has scipy/numpy/PIL, so tests/test_build.py and tests/test_official.py cannot import build. The previous 'python' scripts were already broken (no 'python' on PATH at all), which the python3 switch fixes.
findings.rationale: The DOM test is dependency-free and passes standalone; the render-side dependency gap belongs to build/renderer ownership.

findings.issue: build.py still carries its own page_html/CSS/JS, so site/ keeps the old 9-card page until the renderer imports ui (ui.page_html/ui.CSS/ui.JS, or ui.write_ui(destination, CHARACTERS)).
findings.rationale: build.py is owned by the main agent; page_html raises ValueError if the character list lacks a character a word card needs.

residual_risks: Word buttons link to videos/<char>.mp4 for all 21 characters; if the renderer has not produced the 12 new MP4s yet, those buttons open an empty player. The build-time ValueError only guards the character list, not the presence of files on disk.

jsdom implements neither <dialog> modality nor media playback, so the test stubs showModal/close/play/pause and emulates Escape as cancel->close; native dialog focus restoration and real autoplay policy are not exercised by the test.
